marginalRate.source: TaxTips.ca, 2025 & 2026 Combined Federal & Ontario Tax Rates Including Surtaxes (https://www.taxtips.ca/taxrates/on.htm), checked 2026-10-01. Owner's estimated 2026 taxable income after the planned $53,500 RRSP deduction is about $181,500, in the $181,440-$220,000 combined federal+Ontario bracket taxed at 48.26% on ordinary income. An owner-set estimate, not a filing number.

capitalGainsInclusion.source: Income Tax Act s.38(a); the 2024 proposed increase to 66.67% was deferred (2025-01-31) then cancelled (2025-03-21) by the Department of Finance and confirmed in Budget 2025 (2025-11-04), so the inclusion rate stays 50% for 2026. Checked 2026-10-01 via Scotia Wealth Management, Cancellation of the proposed capital gains inclusion rate increase (https://enrichedthinking.scotiawealthmanagement.com/2025/04/07/cancellation-of-the-proposed-capital-gains-inclusion-rate-increase/).

eligibleDividendGrossUp.source: Income Tax Act s.82(1); 38% gross-up for eligible dividends, unchanged since 2012. Checked 2026-10-01 via wealthnorth.ca Canadian Dividend Tax Credit Guide (https://wealthnorth.ca/taxes/investment-tax/canadian-dividend-tax-credit-guide/).

federalEligibleDtcRate.source: Income Tax Act s.121; federal dividend tax credit of 15.0198% of the grossed-up eligible dividend. Checked 2026-10-01 via wealthnorth.ca Canadian Dividend Tax Credit Guide (https://wealthnorth.ca/taxes/investment-tax/canadian-dividend-tax-credit-guide/).

ontarioEligibleDtcRate.source: Ontario Taxation Act, 2007 s.12; Ontario dividend tax credit of 10% of the grossed-up eligible dividend. Checked 2026-10-01 via wealthnorth.ca Canadian Dividend Tax Credit Guide (https://wealthnorth.ca/taxes/investment-tax/canadian-dividend-tax-credit-guide/).

passiveIncomeRate.source: EY, Corporate investment income tax rates -- 2026 (https://www.ey.com/content/dam/ey-unified-site/ey-com/en-ca/services/tax/tax-calculators/2026/ey-tax-rates-corporate-investment-2026-01-15-v1.pdf), checked 2026-10-01. Combined Ontario CCPC rate on aggregate investment income, before any refund.

partIVRate.source: Income Tax Act Part IV, s.186; 38 1/3% flat rate on portfolio dividends received by a private corporation, long-standing and unchanged for 2026. Checked 2026-10-01.

aaiiThresholds.source: Income Tax Act s.125(5.1); small business deduction grinds by $5 for every $1 of adjusted aggregate investment income (AAII) over $50,000, reaching zero at $150,000. Checked 2026-10-01 via gondaliyacpa.ca Active vs. Passive Income Corporate Tax Implications (https://gondaliyacpa.ca/active-vs-passive-income-corporate-tax-implications/).

nerdtohRate.source: Income Tax Act s.129(4), definition of non-eligible RDTOH; 30.67% of aggregate investment income (AAII) added to non-eligible RDTOH each year. Checked 2026-10-01 via modernaxis.ca RDTOH and ERDTOH: CCPC Investment Income Guide (https://www.modernaxis.ca/blog/rdtoh-erdtoh-ccpc-investment-income).

dividendRefundRate.source: Income Tax Act s.129(1); dividend refund is the lesser of 38.33% of taxable dividends paid and the RDTOH balance. Checked 2026-10-01 via modernaxis.ca RDTOH and ERDTOH: CCPC Investment Income Guide (https://www.modernaxis.ca/blog/rdtoh-erdtoh-ccpc-investment-income).

t1135.source: CRA, Questions and answers about Form T1135 (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/international-non-residents/information-been-moved/foreign-reporting/questions-answers-about-form-t1135.html), checked 2026-10-01. Cost amount (not market value) of specified foreign property; $100,000 filing threshold, $250,000 simplified-vs-detailed reporting method threshold. Both are flat statutory amounts, not indexed.
